placements.title: The asset is the perspective you own, not the substrate you rent
placements.frame: What does this expression say separates intelligence an individual owns from intelligence rented, and where does it locate the asset that lasts when the underlying substrate is interchangeable?
placements.why: The position OwnedVersusRentedIntelligence carries src-2 and src-3, which draw one antithesis: owned versus rented intelligence, substrate as commodity versus perspective as the kept asset. It names a subject future documents will keep feeding, which passes the grain test, and it is a theme, not a one-time fact. The graph is empty, with no leaf to reuse and no close name to inherit from, so this is a NEW mint with no `under` and no lineage.
